A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. All 43 pages, including Appendices A–F, are available and readable; text comparison and rendered-page inspection support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: Appendix F and Figure 1 report original numerical experiments in synthetic tabular, media-streaming, and synthetic linear CMDPs.

after.justification: Appendix F retains the original experiments and Figure 1 results for regret, constraint violations, and safe-policy deployments.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain their procedures and parameters, including C_r = C_u(1 + 2B/xi). The revised confidence and optimism bounds change the analysis, not the algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic tabular, media-streaming, and synthetic linear CMDP scenarios in Appendix F.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Ghosh et al. [18] and the uniform policy appear throughout Figure 1; DOPE appears in the synthetic tabular and media-streaming experiments only.

E3.justification: Appendix F retains identical environment-generation procedures, environment sizes, horizons, constraint thresholds, hyperparameters, and evaluation metrics.

E4.justification: The safe-policy deployment-count analysis in Figure 1 is unchanged. Neither version adds ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or other supplementary empirical analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging Figure 1 over 10 random seeds and display identical shaded bands. Experimental uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figure 1 is visually identical, and Appendix F retains the same numerical curves and qualitative findings. No experimental result entries are added, removed, or revised.

T1.justification: Section 2.2.2 and Appendix D revise reward confidence bounds from C_r to C_u and use the 2BC_u/xi mixture-optimism bonus to make the optimism-gap term nonpositive. The final derivation replaces 4C_r times mixture-policy bonuses with 3C_r times deployed-policy bonuses. These are substantive but localized proof corrections; the stated regret theorems and Appendix E's CMDP proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: computationally efficient exploration in linear CMDPs with sublinear regret and episode-wise safety.

C2.justification: Interpretations of the experiments and regret bounds are unchanged, as are the computational discussion and limitations concerning multiple constraints and adversarial initial states.

D1.justification: Appendix F retains identical implementation descriptions, hyperparameter values, hardware and runtime disclosures, data-generation instructions, and source-code link.

R1.justification: The bibliography, Appendix B, and positioning against previous safe-bandit and CMDP work are unchanged.

P1.justification: Explanatory sentences around Equation (4) and the Appendix D proof are locally rewritten. The title, section order, terminology, and broader narrative remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Shortened and rearranged proof displays change local spacing and page breaks, moving the Appendix E opening onto page 23. Table 1 and Figure 1 retain identical content and presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 removes v3's unsupported application of the cumulative-bonus bound to an unplayed mixture policy, replacing it with a nonpositive optimism-gap argument in Equation (4) and Appendix D. This improves the bandit warm-up proof. The benefit is limited by a newly introduced extra C_u in the explanation of Theorem 5's step (c), inconsistent with its parameter definition. The main CMDP theory and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
